By now everyone in this subverse has heard, seen and possibly played the new Mass Effect game from Bioware and EA. I felt that it was time I reviewed another title here on Voat. I have reviewed at least 2 other games and continue the trend with this new title. I have made comments about this title in other sections of voat and have received both positive and negative reactions.

I currently have 92 hours played total since release day. 3 hours in multiplayer, 66 hours for Singe Player campaign completion(100% minus crew loyalty missions), and 23 hours in New Game + on Hardcore with 70% completion at level 60. I played the 10 hour trial as well but focused more on Multiplayer. I have also completed each of the other 3 Mass Effect titles. I feel comfortable enough to review the title.

The animations. We can start with that and they are shit. No joke, they are the worst I have seen since watching a kid in HS show off his first flash animations. However, for me, this isn't game breaking. Most people see this as a break in immersion. At first it was, however, after time it just became funny. There is a scene at the end of the game that is just so awkwardly funny that you have to start to question what was going on with these people when they animated this stuff. The aliens are great and didn't really have any issues animation wise outside of Peebee and Vera. The humor is great as well and when the animations go to shit and their is a joke in play during conversation it can add to the punch line.

Now that the ugly is out of the way, let me get to the meat of the game. Most will expect Mass Effect to continue the genre of space opera. This isn't the case, and I am glad for it personally. While I enjoyed the story of Shepard and the adventure he provided, I think that the latest installment is trying to move away from the entire space opera feel. I've never played any of the Mass Effects for the story. Shocking to some I am sure. I enjoyed that it was an RPG that was Action oriented and I could shoot people in the face to level up. It was a genre I was wanting for so long and didn't know until my sibling sent me the game and an xbox 360 to play it(let me borrow it to play it). I've never been a huge console fanboy. I play on PC mostly. I then got it on PC and played the entire series. Never for the story, but for the combat. Now, we have a Mass Effect where the combat is the shining moment. I could care less about saving the human race or building a fucking space station. Let me fucking shot kett in the face, warp around the map, be a one punch man one second and then the next a stealthy sniper. People who have only played the 10 hour trial will not even know about this part of the game. Which brings up a point. My second play through on new game plus is much more fun with all the skills, but the enemies are harder, enough that I had to go away from being one punch man. It makes me wonder why they didn't give us more at the beginning. Now, that does bring up a change request that some are asking for which removes the Cool down when you switch profiles. Profiles are a set of 3 abilities and passives that allow you to change skills in combat. When you do, the skills will go on CD. You can't change weapons, but it does allow you flexibility. When I got to this point where I had most of my wanted passives, which was about 20 to 25 hours into the first run I did, I felt the game really pick up. The story started to get better and the challenged kept increasing.

Breakdown:

Graphics: If we exclude animations I would rate it at about an 8. Maybe a little lower, but with the animations it is a 5. 5 for the engine and looking pretty, but the animations to take away from it. I didn't have any FPS issues, however, I am running a decent PC. I played it on Ultra everything, increased field of view, but in 1080p (1920 x 1080) at 144 Hertz. 4K needs some patching from what I have read and buddy who is playing on an AMD rig is only getting like 25 to 40 FPS in 4K. The game ran smooth, and I think I had one FPS issue but it was because of the huge battle at the end of the game. I mean huge. The other issue is repeated character models, specifically the Asari. They took a huge shortcut here, but I am starting to wonder if they are all clones. There are a lot of clone themes in this game. So that might be on purpose. There were a couple of lighting glitches, but I didn't have any hard crashes. The game was stable. The only time I had any issue was in multiplayer but they were known issues, one has been fixed, other is being resolved currently.

Sound and Music: There were some issues with sound in the trial, but have been patched since. The music adds to the game and the combat, but doesn't drown out your team so you can hear them talk. Sounds are pretty crisp, but somethings are really weird, like sliding rocks and other stuff share the same sound.

Replay ability: With the New Game Plus, for those who make the journey, you will find that after you beat the game you can start again, however, you will lose out on rank 6 loyalty mission rewards until you do them again, and you lose all your AVP. Outside of that, pretty much all carries over. You even learn higher level research. Once I got 20 hours in the game picked up.

I remember the first Mass Effect, when my sibling sent me the console I almost sent it back at first because the game was so slow. I didn't want to play a movie, I wanted to play a game. Then I sat down and actually played it, once I got the Normandy and was able to set off where I wanted the game opened up and I was hooked. I think the same applies to Mass Effect Andromeda.

Multiplayer: Just like Mass Effect 3, but better. Personally I would have bought the Multiplayer as a standalone game. It gets addictive.

Score: 74 out of 100.

Final Thoughts: Should you buy this game? Wait for a sale. I have never told anyone to go out and buy this title. Now, Horizon: Zero Dawn and Nioh, you should go buy those asap if you have a PS4. The only discussion I have had on voat in regards to Mass Effect Andromeda center around the saying, "Never judge a book by it's cover". If the title is on sale for 30 bucks I would say buy it. Personally, I got my moneys worth out of this title. I am still playing and will continue as I have barely touched multiplayer. For all it's flaws, underneath the bad animations, lays a decent game. Let us hope they will learn that office politics and PC bullshit in game development doesn't equate to a fantastic triple A game. I don't think they will, and those who boycott this title or bash me for the review, will not change anything either. EA is a massive game with far reaching arms in gaming world. This game will not change anything and thinking that you can change it with your wallet is just wishful thinking. If EA was a smaller gaming company then I would think it could, but they have so many other titles that will make the money back for them. It would take an entire EA boycott and that isn't going to happen anytime soon. While the game has it's flaws, I think the meat of the game makes up for the issues that are on the surface. Luckily Bioware has acknowledged these issues and are working to fix them. Until next time Goats, keep on gaming.
